Most of these reviews are written by people that have never really played a proper simulator before. They go in expecting arcade style controls and are put off by a Newtonian physics model that feels clunky to them. The game has a pretty awesome flight model once you understand it.

The real problem is that to get the most out of this game you really need to be playing with a joystick that at minimum has a z-axis (twist handle) so that you get proper yaw, pitch, and roll control. You also would do well to have a hat or other control for your vertical and lateral thrusters, as well as some kind of analog throttle control as these all contribute to your manoeuvrability. Optimally you want a full HOTAS to really get immersed. It's very hard to be competitive in this game with a mouse and a keyboard and gamepads while better due to having analog sticks still fall short.

Advanced flight in Elite has a pretty steep learning curve that takes some time to learn. The game does benefit from VR, or even just head tracking but it's really not necessary.
